accuracy.where: What you need, Checkpoint command-not-found: "A new window picks up the folder the installer put `claude` in." (line 62). Also line 64 "The old window just hasn't seen the new command." and Final test spot-unneeded-step, line 295 "A new window is what lets the terminal find `claude`"
accuracy.problem: The advice (try a new window first) is right, but the reason given is wrong. The native installer never adds its folder to PATH, so a new window only helps if that folder is already on PATH. On a stock Mac with zsh, ~/.local/bin usually isn't, so the new window fails too. The reader learns that the installer set PATH up, and the Final test feedback repeats it as fact.
accuracy.evidence: troubleshoot-install docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install, read 2026-10-24), Verify your PATH: the installer reports `Native installation exists but ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH.` under `Setup notes:` and "prints the fix with that note but doesn't change PATH itself." setup docs: "open a new terminal window and run `claude --version` ... If your shell says `claude` isn't found ... the install directory isn't on your PATH yet".
accuracy.fix: Line 62: "> Right. The docs say to check in a new window first. If it's still missing, the installer didn't put its folder on your PATH (the list of folders your terminal searches for commands): its 'Setup notes' print the fix, and the install troubleshooting docs explain it." Line 64: "> Don't reinstall yet. First rule out the old window, then check the installer's Setup notes about PATH." Line 295: "> The docs say to check the install in a new window, and the version number proves it worked."

reader.where: What you need, Claude Code bullet, "Then open a new terminal window and run `claude --version`." (line 33); terminal Scene caption "A version number means it worked." (line 42); Try step 1 "install it (see What you need), then open a new terminal window" (line 183); Cheat sheet "`claude --version`, in a new window" (line 254)
reader.problem: Everywhere the reader is meant to look, the Lesson says a new window is all it takes. On a default Mac or Windows machine that's often not enough. The installer puts `claude` in a folder that isn't on PATH and doesn't add it, so a new window still says "command not found". The only place the Lesson says what to do next (run the line under "Setup notes") is inside the command-not-found Checkpoint's closed answer box (line 62). A Visitor who never opens that box gets stuck before the Try, or keeps reopening windows and reinstalling. The Mac Scene also shows a new window working first time, which a fresh Mac may not do.
reader.evidence: troubleshoot-install (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install, Verify your PATH): the installer "places `claude` at `~/.local/bin/claude` on macOS/Linux or `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe` on Windows". It reports a missing PATH entry under "Setup notes:" and "prints the fix with that note but doesn't change PATH itself." The default PATH list on this Mac (`cat /etc/paths`) is only /usr/local/bin, /System/Cryptexes/App/usr/bin, /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin and /sbin, with no ~/.local/bin. The setup page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) says that if `claude` still isn't found after the new window, "the install directory isn't on your PATH yet". In the Lesson, only line 62 (Checkpoint feedback) mentions Setup notes.
reader.fix: Line 33: after "Then open a new terminal window and run `claude --version`." add "Still not found? Run the line the installer printed under "Setup notes", then open another window." (+15 prose words). To stay under the 1,400 cap (now 1,386), shorten line 93 to "Read them in order the first time." (−7). Scene caption at line 42 (captions don't count toward the budget): "# Open a new terminal window, then check it. A version number means it worked. If it says "command not found", run the line the installer printed under "Setup notes", then open another window." Try step 1: "If either isn't found, install it and open a new terminal window (see What you need, including the Setup notes line for `claude`)."

reader.where: Try it yourself, step 5 and its check (lines 206–225): "mkdir ~/learn-git", "Answer its questions, then type `/exit`.", "`ls` in `~/learn-git` lists `MISSION.md`"
reader.problem: Step 5 has three gaps for someone who barely uses a terminal. Starting `claude` in a new folder brings the trust question back, but only step 2 says to choose Yes. Nothing says when it's safe to exit: `/teach` writes MISSION.md only after the mission interview, then keeps working on sources and a lesson, so exiting right after the last answer can leave the check failing. Finally, `ls` and `~` are never explained.

The words `ls` and `~` appear only in commands and checks, never with a clause.
reader.fix: After the step 5 code block: "When it asks whether you trust this folder, choose Yes. Then type:". Line 219: "Answer its questions. These add about 25 prose words, so pair them with cuts elsewhere.
